bibliographic_identity.title: Cash Got Your Tongue? CEO Language-Uncertainty Around Undisclosed Cash Acquisitions
bibliographic_identity.author: Sina Soleimanipour
bibliographic_identity.degree: Master of Science in Management (Thesis based)
bibliographic_identity.institution: Telfer School of Management, University of Ottawa

study_scope.setting: United States public, non-financial, non-utility firms
study_scope.primary_language_setting: CEO answers in the unscripted question-and-answer segment of quarterly earnings calls
study_scope.deal_source_and_definition: SDC acquisitions with known payment composition and transaction value of at least $1 million; at least 50 percent cash defines the cash arm and at least 50 percent stock defines the stock comparison arm.

thesis_digest.study_purpose_from_thesis: Ask whether chief-executive question-and-answer uncertainty tracks a deal's passage from private to public, meaning whether it is elevated while an acquisition is withheld and recedes once it is announced.
thesis_digest.approved_plain_language_central_message: Before a company announces a cash acquisition, its CEO's unscripted answers become unusually uncertain. The uncertainty disappears once the deal becomes public, even though the cash remains until closing. This pattern is stronger for cash deals than for stock deals.

research_questions.approved_wording: Is residual CEO Q&A uncertainty elevated in the pre-announcement quarter of cash acquirers relative to those firms' other quarters?
Does residual uncertainty resolve at announcement while the acquirer's cash persists until completion?
research_questions.maps_to_analysis: MA2: Differential Timing Around the Announcement

research_questions.approved_wording: Is the pre-announcement uncertainty run-up stronger for cash acquirers than for stock acquirers?

hypotheses_as_stated_in_thesis.statement: Residual chief-executive Q&A uncertainty is elevated in the pre-announcement quarter of cash acquirers, relative to those same firms' other quarters.
The pre-announcement uncertainty run-up is stronger for cash acquirers than for stock acquirers.
Residual Q&A uncertainty resolves at the announcement, falling even before the deal closes, while the acquirer's cash persists until it is paid at completion.

key_constructs.name: UncAnsCEO
key_constructs.definition: The number of Loughran-McDonald uncertainty words used by the CEO in answers divided by the CEO's total answer words.

key_constructs.name: UncResCEO
key_constructs.definition: The call-level residual from the Dzielinski, Wagner, and Zeckhauser style decomposition re-estimated on the thesis sample. It is CEO answer uncertainty remaining after persistent CEO style, other call-language measures, firm-performance controls, and year effects are removed.

key_constructs.name: CashRatio
key_constructs.definition: Cash and equivalents divided by total assets.

key_constructs.name: PreAnnounceQtr
key_constructs.definition: Indicator equal to one in event quarter e = -1, the call quarter immediately before the acquisition announcement quarter.

key_constructs.name: CashScrutiny
key_constructs.definition: The percentage share of analyst Q&A turns devoted to cash and liquidity.

main_findings.title: Pre-announcement run-up
main_findings.approved_simple_statement: CEO residual Q&A uncertainty rises before cash acquisitions are announced.
main_findings.interpretive_boundary: The design documents a within-firm pre-announcement mean shift. It does not identify a causal effect.

main_findings.title: Differential timing around announcement
main_findings.approved_simple_statement: Residual uncertainty disappears when the deal is announced, while the cash remains until completion.
main_findings.source_section: Main Analysis 2: Differential Timing Around the Announcement
main_findings.interpretive_boundary: Cash persistence through the gap is inferred from the absence of a PRE1-to-GAP decline. The GAP cash coefficient itself is positive but not significant. Cash falling only at completion is partly mechanical.

main_findings.title: Cash concentration
main_findings.approved_simple_statement: The pre-announcement uncertainty run-up is stronger for cash acquisitions than for stock acquisitions.
main_findings.interpretive_boundary: The formal result is supported but fragile because the difference partly rides on an imprecise negative stock estimate. Use concentration or stronger for cash, not strict specificity. The proposed war-chest mechanism is not established.

overall_interpretive_boundaries: The evidence is descriptive, correlational, and identified through within-firm comparisons with calendar-time controls.
The design supports no causal identification and establishes no mechanism.
Compliance-constrained silence and strategically chosen silence are observationally equivalent in the data.
The cash build-up mechanism is motivated but not identified.
The stock-financed comparison shares the disclosure bind but is an imperfect counterfactual.
The uncertainty measure is a finance-specific word-list operationalization that abstracts from context.
The residual is available only for CEOs with at least five calls, creating selection toward larger and better-covered firms.
The 2002 to 2018 U.S. public-firm sample may not generalize to other periods, markets, or smaller firms.
UncResCEO is a generated regressand, so the two-step standard-error concern must be acknowledged.
Some thesis tables report focal tests one-tailed, but the load-bearing pre-announcement run-up survives a two-tailed test.

additional_analyses_for_appendix_only.thesis_conclusion: Measured analyst cash scrutiny does not account for this pre-announcement run-up, but the test is an underpowered failure to find rather than a formal equivalence test.
UncResCEO is unrelated to the post-call spread, while scripted presentation uncertainty is contemporaneously positively associated with it in several one-tailed specifications.
Treating withdrawal as a resolution event leaves the round-trip pattern in place, though few additional observations enter.
The cash timing conclusion survives removal of the lagged dependent variable.

The run-up, differential timing, and formal cash concentration survive when all deals are stacked. Forward linear-probability and logit forms provide additional associations, with appropriate caveats.
